extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or graduate students and researchers in enumerative combinatorics studying posets, P-partitions, and related algebraic/combinatorial invariants
extracted.subtask_description: Understand definitions, structural properties, and generating-function/reciprocity results for labelled posets: R-labelings, (P,ω)-partitions, order polynomials, Eulerian posets, and toric h/g-polynomials, with examples and combinatorial interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: βL(S) for distributive lattices (Theorem 3.13.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L = J(P) be a finite distributive lattice of rank n with a natural labeling ω. For S ⊆ [n−1], βL(S) equals the number of permutations w in the Jordan-Hölder set (P, ω) whose descent set is S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof gives explicit bijection: arrange labels of successive order ideals in increasing order to form permutations; αL(S) equals number of chains of order ideals with prescribed sizes. Example: for a naturally labelled poset the Jordan-Hölder set may be listed and βL(S) computed directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-analogue for Bn(q) (Theorem 3.13.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For L = Bn(q), the lattice of subspaces of Fn_q, βL(S) = sum_{w∈Sn, D(w)=S} q^{inv(w)}, i.e., the q-weighted count of permutations with descent set S where inv(w) is number of inversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare αL(S) computed via q-binomial factors (product of Gaussian binomial coefficients) to the formula from Chapter 2 (equation (2.20)); examples follow by matching terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-labeling (Definition 3.14.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-labeling of a finite graded poset P with ˆ0 and ˆ1 is a function λ on the cover relations H(P) such that for every interval [s,t] there is a unique saturated chain s = t0 ⋖ t1 ⋖ … ⋖ tℓ = t with labels nondecreasing: λ(t0,t1) ≤ λ(t1,t2) ≤ … ≤ λ(t_{ℓ−1},tℓ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poset possessing an R-labeling is called R-labelable or an R-poset; the unique chain is called the increasing chain. Intervals inherit R-labelings by restriction. Examples: natural labelings of J(P), supersolvable lattices with an M-chain (formula (3.56)), semimodular lattices (formula (3.57)), and even some non-lattices (Figure 3.28).

rubrics_metrics.name: βP(S) via R-labelings (Theorem 3.14.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is an R-poset of rank n with R-labeling λ, then for S ⊆ [n−1], βP(S) equals the number of maximal chains m of P whose sequence of labels λ(m) = (λ(t0,t1),...,λ(t_{n−1},t_n)) has descent set S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs, for any partial chain with specified descent positions, a unique maximal chain whose label-descent set contains S; thus α′P(S)=αP(S) and β′P(S)=βP(S). This gives a direct combinatorial interpretation and is used in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersolvable lattice and M-chain characterization (Example 3.14.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite lattice L is supersolvable if it possesses a maximal chain c (an M-chain) such that the sublattice generated by c and any other chain is distributive. For such L an explicit R-labeling λ is given by λ(s,t)=min{i: s∨t_i = t} where t_i are elements of the M-chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: modular lattices, partition lattice Π_n, lattices of subgroups of finite supersolvable groups. The R-labeling on the distributive sublattice generated by c and another chain coincides with the natural-label R-labeling from Example 3.14.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semimodular lattices are R-posets (Example 3.14.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite (upper) semimodular lattice L, label the join-irreducibles t_i via an order-preserving bijection ω and define λ(s,t)=min{i: s∨t_i = t}; this λ is an R-labeling, so semimodular lattices are R-posets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 3.27 gives an example with computed maximal-chain labels and descent-set counts; the construction depends on identifying join-irreducibles and their indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: (P,ω)-partition definition (3.15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (P,ω)-partition is a function σ:P→N that is order-reversing (s ≤ t in P implies σ(s) ≥ σ(t)), and for s < t with ω(s) > ω(t) the inequality is strict σ(s) > σ(t). If σ(P) includes n as the maximum value we say σ is a (P,ω)-partition of n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: natural labelings give ordinary P-partitions (order-reversing), dual natural give strict P-partitions. This definition interpolates partitions and compositions by using P to impose inequalities and ω to impose strictness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental generating function FP,ω (Definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: FP,ω(x1,...,xp) = ∑_{σ} x_{1}^{σ(t1)} x_{2}^{σ(t2)} ··· x_{p}^{σ(tp)}, sum over all (P,ω)-partitions σ: P→N, where t1,...,tp are the elements of P in label order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FP,ω encodes all information about (P,ω)-partitions; examples for chains and antichains yield explicit product formulas (rational functions). Knowing FP,ω determines (P,ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition by linear extensions (Lemma 3.15.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of (P,ω)-partitions equals the disjoint union over linear extensions w in the Jordan-Hölder set L(P,ω) of Sw, where Sw is the set of σ whose σ′ is w-compatible (σ′ reindexes by labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma underlies the decomposition of FP,ω into simpler pieces corresponding to each linear extension; it is the combinatorial basis for subsequent product formulas (each block corresponds to a rational factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for Fw (Lemma 3.15.4 / equation 3.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a linear extension w with associated label permutation w′, the generating function Fw equals ∏_{i=1}^p 1/(1 - x_{w′_1} x_{w′_2} ··· x_{w′_i}) times a prefactor x_{w′_1}^{D(w)}? (explicit product expression in Lemma 3.15.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive proof via compositions: define nonnegative ci differences according to descents of w, establishing a bijection between terms; this yields an explicit rational factor for each w. (See equation (3.59) and the proof for exact indexing conventions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Main expansion of FP,ω (Theorem 3.15.5, equation 3.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: FP,ω(x1,...,xp) = ∑_{w∈L(P,ω)} ( ∏_{j∈D(w)} x_{w′_1}···x_{w′_j} ) / ∏_{i=1}^p (1 - x_{w′_1}···x_{w′_i} ), i.e., FP,ω is the sum over linear extensions of explicit rational factors determined by descents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formula follows by combining the decomposition lemma and the explicit forms for each Fw; Example 3.15.6 shows assembling the terms for a concrete labelled poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization GP,ω(x) and WP,ω(x) (Theorem 3.15.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: GP,ω(x) = ∑_{n≥0} a(n) x^n = FP,ω(x,x,...,x) has the form WP,ω(x) / ∏_{i=1}^p (1 - x^i), where WP,ω(x) = ∑_{w∈L(P,ω)} x^{maj(w)} is a polynomial (the numerator) called WP,ω(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus GP is a rational function with polynomial numerator WP given by summing x^{maj(w)} over linear extensions; WP degree equals δ(P) (Corollary 3.15.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity for (P,ω)-partitions (Theorem 3.15.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ω̄ be the complementary labeling ω̄(t) = p+1 − ω(t). Then as rational functions FP,ω(x1,...,xp) and FP,ω̄ satisfy x1x2···xp FP,ω(x1,...,xp) = (−1)^p FP,ω̄(1/x1,...,1/xp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 3.15.9 proves the analogous identity for each Fw; global reciprocity follows by summing over linear extensions. Consequences include reciprocal identities for GP,ω, WP,ω, HP,ω, and AP,ω (equations (3.67)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order polynomial ΩP,ω(m) and HP,ω(x) correspondence (Theorem 3.15.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order polynomial ΩP,ω(m) := # of (P,ω)-partitions σ:P→{1..m} is a degree-p polynomial in m; its generating function HP,ω(x) = ∑_{m≥0} ΩP,ω(m) x^m satisfies HP,ω(x) = ∑_{w∈L(P,ω)} x^{1+des(w)} / (1 - x)^{p+1} (equation (3.65)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently define the (P,ω)-Eulerian polynomial AP,ω(x) = ∑_{w∈L(P,ω)} x^{1+des(w)}. Coefficients of HP yield Ω values and relate to Eulerian statistics on linear extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: δ(t) and δ-chain condition; symmetry of WP (Definitions and Theorem 3.15.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: For naturally labelled P, δ(t) is length of longest chain starting at t. δ(P) = max_t δ(t). P satisfies the δ-chain condition if all principal dual order ideals V_t have maximal chains of equal length. P satisfies δ-chain condition iff WP(x) satisfies x^{(p choose 2) − δ(P)} WP(1/x) = WP(x) (i.e., WP is palindromic up to shift).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an explicit bijection σ → σ′: σ′(t)=σ(t)+δ(t) between P-partitions and strict P-partitions if and only if the δ-chain condition holds (Lemma 3.15.15). Example and proof show how generating functions encode the condition as x^{δ(P)}GP(x)=GP(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: λ-chain condition, gradedness, and order-polynomial bijections (Lemma 3.15.17 and Corollary 3.15.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ℓ be length of longest chains. Define injections θ_i: A_ℓ(P) → A_{ℓ+i}(P) by θ_i(σ)=σ+δ. Then θ_1 bijective iff P satisfies the λ-chain condition (every element lies in a maximum-length chain). θ_1 and θ_2 bijective iff P is graded; in graded case θ_i bijective for all i. Consequences: evaluations of ΩP at small integers and equivalent conditions for gradedness are given in Corollary 3.15.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these bijections to deduce vanishing and sign properties of ΩP(m) at small integer arguments and to detect gradedness from few values of ΩP (practical computational use in Example 3.15.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eulerian poset definition and Möbius sign alternation
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite graded poset P with ˆ0 and ˆ1 is Eulerian if µ_P(s,t) = (−1)^{ℓ(s,t)} for all s < t in P (i.e., Möbius function alternates by rank).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eulerian posets have many chain-enumeration duality properties; several propositions in the section derive consequences for multichain enumerators Z(P,m) and for βP(S) symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z(P,m) reciprocity/properties for Eulerian and simplicial posets (Propositions 3.16.1 & 3.16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is Eulerian of rank n then Z(P,m) satisfies a sign reciprocity (variant: Z(P,m) = (−1)^n Z(P,−m) in the text). If P is simplicial (each interval [ˆ0,t] ≅ boolean algebra), then Z(P,m)=∑_{i≥0} W_i · (m choose i) with sign adjustments where W_i is number of t with [ˆ0,t] ≅ B_i; in graded case Z(P,q+1) is the rank-generating function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining both facts yields relations (Dehn–Sommerville type) among the W_i's (equation (3.73)); examples for small ranks list the linear relations explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: βP(S) duality for Eulerian posets (Proposition 3.16.5 & Corollary 3.16.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Eulerian poset P of rank n+1 and any subposet Q containing ˆ0 and ˆ1, µ_Q(ˆ0,ˆ1) = (−1)^n µ_Q(ˆ0,ˆ1) when Q is taken as complement-type subposet (precise statement in Prop. 3.16.5). In particular, for S ⊆ [n−1] we have β_P(S) = β_P(S^c) (palindromicity/complementarity of flag h-vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use Möbius inversion, alternating signs from Eulerian property, and iterated removal of elements; topological viewpoint via Alexander duality is discussed to motivate the stronger homological statements (Gorenstein* posets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Toric f- and g-polynomials (Definitions (3.74)–(3.76))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Eulerian poset P (rank n+1) define inductively f(P,x) (toric h-polynomial) and g(P,x) (toric g-polynomial): base f(1)=g(1)=1; write f(P,x)=h_0+...+h_n x^n and set g(P,x)=h_0 + (h_1−h_0)x + (h_2−h_1)x^2 + ... up to floor(n/2) differences; then set f(P,x)=∑_{Q≤P} g(Q,x) (x−1)^{n−ρ(Q)} (equation (3.76)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute recursively on intervals [ˆ0,t] ordered by inclusion; examples: boolean algebra B_n gives f(B_n,x)=1+x+...+x^n and g(B_n,x)=1. The polynomials encode deep duality and symmetry properties of Eulerian posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry of toric f-polynomial for Eulerian posets (Theorem 3.16.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Eulerian poset P of rank n+1, f(P,x) satisfies f(P,x) = x^n f(P,1/x); equivalently the toric h-vector (h_0,...,h_n) is palindromic with h_i = h_{n−i}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the defining recurrences, Möbius inversion, the Eulerian property (sign alternation), and induction on rank. Examples computed earlier illustrate palindromicity.
